question.prompt: Which of the following polynomials has the greatest real root?

solutions.title: Compare increasing polynomials
solutions.explanation:
The productive observation is that we can compare the locations of the roots without solving for them. Write \(f_A,f_B,f_C,f_D,f_E\) for the five polynomials.

Every odd power of \(x\) is strictly increasing on the real line. Thus each listed polynomial is strictly increasing. For choices A through D, the values at \(-1\) and \(0\) are \(-2018\) and \(1\); for E, they are \(-1\) and \(2018\). By continuity and strict increase, each polynomial has exactly one real root, and it lies in \((-1,0)\).

On this interval, increasing an odd exponent makes the power less negative. In particular,
\[
x^{19}>x^{17},\qquad x^{13}>x^{11}.
\]
It follows that
\[
f_C(x)>f_A(x)>f_B(x),\qquad f_D(x)>f_B(x).
\]
At the root of \(f_B\), the other three polynomials are positive. Since they are increasing, their roots must lie to its left. This eliminates A, C, and D.

To compare with E, first note that \(0<x^6<1\), so
\[
x^6+2018>2019x^6.
\]
Multiplying by \(x^{11}<0\) reverses the inequality, giving
\[
f_B(x)=x^{11}(x^6+2018)+1<2019x^{17}+1.
\]
The root of E is
\[
r_E=-\frac{2018}{2019}=-\left(1-\frac1{2019}\right).
\]
We use Bernoulli's inequality, \((1-u)^n\ge 1-nu\) for \(0<u<1\) and positive integers \(n\). For completeness, the case \(n=1\) is equality, and the induction step is
\[
(1-u)^{n+1}\ge(1-nu)(1-u)
=1-(n+1)u+nu^2\ge1-(n+1)u.
\]
Applying this with \(u=\tfrac1{2019}\) and \(n=17\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
f_B(r_E)
&<1-2019\left(1-\frac1{2019}\right)^{17}\\
&\le1-2019\left(1-\frac{17}{2019}\right)\\
&=-2001<0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(f_B\) is increasing, its root lies to the right of \(r_E\) as well. Therefore the polynomial with the greatest real root is
\[
\boxed{x^{17}+2018x^{11}+1},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
